About the Position

Frankfurt's IMPRS Cellular Biophysics programme is preparing its next recruitment call. Hosted by Max Planck Society in Frankfurt. Apply by Next call: winter 2026/27; exact deadline not announced. No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is required; English is assessed through the application and interviews.

Upcoming Recruitment Round

This record describes the next call rather than an application window confirmed open. The next cohort is planned for September 2027, with the winter 2026/27 application window and final deadline to be announced on the official page.

About the Project

Frankfurt's IMPRS Cellular Biophysics programme is preparing its next recruitment call. The programme focuses on the physical and biological processes of cells. Applications are expected from December 2026, but the next closing date has not been announced. This PhD opening at Max Planck Society centres on IMPRS Cellular Biophysics PhD, Frankfurt: Next Call. The work sits within Physics, Biology. The role is based in Frankfurt, Germany. This is a fully funded opportunity; financial support is listed as Approx. €3,010/month gross (TV-L E13, 65% — typical doctoral level). Interested candidates should note the deadline: 21 January 2027, 23:59 CET (2027 call).

Research Areas

  • Cellular biophysics
  • Biology
  • Physics

Funding and Duration

ComponentDetails
Award or positionPhD scholarship / studentship
Stipend / salaryDoctoral funding; exact amount not stated

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants provide an overview of their bachelor’s and master’s studies, describe their research experience, upload the required documents and give referee contact details. Candidates are advised to review the school’s published eligibility criteria before applying.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Recruitment statusUpcoming: applications expected December 2026
Deadline / consideration roundNext closing date not announced
LocationGermany

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Next call: winter 2026/27; exact - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Review the official programme page and check the opening date for the next call.
  2. Use the new call to select a project or research area and identify the documents required for that application route.
  3. Complete the submission when the application window opens, using the new deadline rather than an earlier recruitment cycle.

About Max Planck Society

The Max Planck Society operates research institutes and International Max Planck Research Schools in Germany. Doctoral candidates work within a selected institute or partner university, with funding and supervision arranged through the programme or project.

Official details: Read the programme or project information

Application route: Follow the official application instructions

Application guides

  • How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps

English language requirements

This structured German doctoral programme does not ask for IELTS or TOEFL scores at admission; the programme runs in English and proficiency is assessed through your written application, references and interviews. You can include a test score if you have one, but its absence does not weaken an application.

Official Link
